dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No escalation."
"pull a read-only sample of 3–5 underlying dealer receipts from the May batch to cross-check effective_event_date against source documents."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "fully explained" and "contractually-permitted monthly batch cycle" overstate the evidence because the underlying contract was not provided and the email's explanation is only corroboration.

"not duplicate revenue" is stronger than the demonstrated tests support: absence of duplicate source_event_id or recharge_id does not by itself rule out duplicate cash or entitlement records represented by distinct IDs.

"This hypothesis would only survive if any of those three fields were nonzero/mismatched" overstates what the import-log fields can rule out; a pipeline defect could still affect downstream analytics or other untested transformations.
"not manipulated reporting" is appropriately qualified later, but the initial categorical rejection is stronger than the available dealer-side source evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the main benign alternative well: two dealers may submit annual-plan events in month-end batches while retaining original effective dates. The strongest missed alternative is a non-duplicate-ID financial or entitlement issue, or a downstream event-time analytics distortion, that would not necessarily appear in duplicate-ID or import-log reconciliation fields.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly test duplicate cash and entitlement impact, and add a downstream safeguard stating that retention and event-time analytics must use effective_event_date rather than posted_at; then narrow the conclusion to no material issue only for the tested dealer batches.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "the case-creation collapse (49.5%→3.3%) plus the pre-auth exclusion rule drive most of the visible drop"
"new balance/pack self-service stages (absent under LEGACY) plausibly drive a genuine minority of it"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "CAUSAL CLAIMS (tentative)" and "UNKNOWNS: whether affected subscribers call back later; the formal containment metric definition; what operationally happens to a failed pre-auth session today"
"NOVA and LEGACY session counts are directly comparable... NOVA logs roughly 12x more sessions per month, so raw rate comparisons without accounting for the logging change are misleading."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally on this evidence."
"Keep the South pilot running as-is (reversible) rather than pausing or expanding it."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Add an all-contact containment number and a pre-auth abandonment rate to the dashboard"
"Unknowns that would change the call"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the case-creation collapse (49.5%→3.3%) plus the pre-auth exclusion rule drive most of the visible drop" is a plausible mechanism but "most" is not quantitatively established by the supplied evidence.

"that gap is suppression, not resolution" overstates what can be inferred from steady outage counts and falling NO_SIGNAL cases; service events and complaint cases are not one-to-one, and falling NO_SIGNAL cases could have multiple explanations.
"some deflection is genuine" is plausible from the new self-service stages, but stage completion alone does not demonstrate successful resolution or improved customer experience.
The claim that 175 subscribers "never resolved in a later NOVA session" does not establish that they remained unresolved overall, since they may have succeeded through another session or channel.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the strongest competing interpretation that some of the decline reflects genuine self-service, explicitly attributing a "genuine minority" to new balance and pack stages. It missed a fuller benign interpretation of pre-auth abandonment: some abandoned sessions may reflect non-complaint contacts, successful resolution outside the logged NOVA path, or users who no longer needed help, so abandonment and missing case creation should not be treated as unresolved customer friction without journey linkage or sampled call review.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete the proposed end-to-end validation by linking pre-auth failures to repeat contacts and downstream outcomes, and sample/listen to affected calls; this would test whether missing cases represent unresolved complaints rather than merely unobserved or non-problem contacts.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Observed claims are tied specifically to inverter_events.csv: “4 events, 27 May–4 Jun, 4 distinct inverters, one event each, no recurrence.”
Observed claims are tied to named fields: “impact_mw=0, cleared=yes, severity info/warning only, duration ≤7 min.”
The submission distinguishes the inferred representativeness concern from the observed event rows and explicitly notes that completeness cannot be confirmed from the file alone.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst uses multiple fields together—impact, cleared status, severity, duration, inverter distinctness, and recurrence—to reject escalation rather than relying only on event names.
The analyst tests the equipment-problem interpretation against measurable outcomes: “none of the measurable columns support it.”
The reasoning does not substantially test independent channels or alternative benign mechanisms beyond the CSV, so it falls short of fully triangulated investigation.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission assigns claim-specific confidence: “Confidence: Medium” for coverage and “Confidence: High” for the direct row-level observations.
It clearly states the material unknown: “nothing in the file states whether this is the full export or a filtered slice.”
It requests the smallest decision-changing evidence—date/entity filter and same-window plant event count—and limits the conclusion to representativeness rather than claiming a fleet-wide baseline.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Do not escalate” follows from zero impact, cleared status, low severity, short duration, and lack of recurrence.
The proposed action is a cheap, discriminating metadata check: “confirm this export's date/entity filter and compare against the plant's logged event count for the same window.”
The stopping rule—“If that check shows it's the complete, unfiltered export, stop there”—is proportionate and preserves the relevant operational constraint.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from short, cleared, zero-impact warnings.
It appropriately treats sparse coverage as the only remaining qualification rather than escalating mixed event wording into a fault hypothesis.
The conclusion is accurately scoped to this export and does not claim that the file proves all fleet behavior.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Nothing here is a live fault” is slightly stronger than the evidence supports: cleared events and zero impact show no current recorded operational impact, but do not prove that no underlying equipment issue existed.
“That's consistent with routine telemetry” is a reasonable inference, not a direct observation; the submission generally signals this appropriately, but it should avoid treating it as definitive.
“The alarm is in the wording only” overstates the case somewhat, since the event names could still reflect genuine transient conditions even though the supplied fields do not support escalation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be incomplete or filtered, so four isolated zero-impact events cannot establish that the plant had no broader recurring issue. A second, lower-concern interpretation is that the event names represent transient communications or equipment-condition alerts that cleared without generation loss; this would still support no escalation absent recurrence, impact, or persistence.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly distinguish “no live operational impact” from “no underlying fault,” and state that the proposed completeness check is the only evidence needed before stopping; if the export is complete, no further mechanism investigation is warranted.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Recomputing directly from `dispatch_blocks.csv`: 28 May penalty Rs 662,444, 29 May penalty Rs 453,086 — a 31.6% drop"; the submission identifies the field and aggregation used.

"`base_schedule_mw` is the pre-pilot schedule... Holding actual generation fixed and recomputing 29 May's penalty... gives Rs 549,664 vs Rs 453,086"; this directly addresses the required same-day counterfactual.
The evidence table also cites firmware, weather, block counts, DSM band rates, and energy pricing, distinguishing observed data from causal limitations.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes the cross-day comparison from the within-day base-versus-submitted comparison rather than accepting the 31.6% headline.
It tests plausible alternative explanations by comparing weather, firmware, stow-block counts, the banded penalty mechanism, energy value, and the possibility of hindsight adjustment.

"Still causally unidentified" explicitly limits generalization, ex-ante forecast-skill claims, and net commercial value rather than treating the mechanical recalculation as a complete causal analysis.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "That's the defensible number, not 31.6%, and it's identified from only one pilot day" appropriately narrows the claim.
"The estimate still rests on a single day and on penalty alone" and the request to confirm revisions preceded actual generation show claim-specific uncertainty.

The submission preserves a smaller apparent benefit rather than overcorrecting to no effect, while explicitly noting that the same-day calculation does not establish generalization or hindsight-free skill.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Keep the pilot running as a low-cost evaluation... but report the ~17.6% within-day figure... and do not expand beyond the pilot yet" follows the evidence and preserves the possibility of value.
The proposed next test—repeated base-versus-submitted comparisons on high-wind days, firmware control, net commercial value, and timing verification—is discriminating rather than generic.
The recommendation correctly identifies net value, not DSM penalty alone, as the decision-relevant outcome.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately states that 31.6% is a cross-day comparison and that the same-day modeled difference is approximately 17.6%.
It retains the legitimate finding that the pilot day performed better under the mechanical counterfactual while rejecting the unsupported claim that the pilot caused a generalized 31.6% reduction.
The conclusion is consistent with the supplied dynamics: favorable direction, but insufficient matched events for a controlled causal estimate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling 28 May a "cherry-picked baseline" implies intentional selection; the evidence establishes that it was the worst day and that the comparison is cross-day, but not the decision-maker's intent.

Calling `base_schedule_mw` an "identical, non-pilot schedule" is operationally useful but should be described more precisely as a recorded pre-pilot/base schedule; it is not by itself proof of the schedule that would have been submitted absent the pilot.
The phrase "within-day effect" could be read causally. It is better characterized as a same-day mechanical penalty difference conditional on holding actual generation fixed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The approximately 17.6% reduction may reflect a hindsight-adjusted schedule or a tradeoff against scheduled-energy value rather than genuine forecast skill or improved net commercial performance. It is therefore a useful conditional billing calculation, but not yet a causal estimate of pilot value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the timestamps showing that all 12 schedule revisions were submitted before actual generation was known, then repeat the base-versus-submitted and net-value analysis across multiple comparable high-wind days with firmware held constant.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses - \"90211000 is a keying error for 90211090\" — rejected: it's Switzerland's own current code, not a mistyped Helios value."
"\"Helios is authoritative, so the declaration is wrong\" — rejected: Helios is disclaimed as non-ruling commercial data."
"\"A mismatch flag means an error\" — rejected: schema has no code-system/version field, so it can't tell a real error from two valid codes in different systems."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Confidence" is explicitly recorded for each evidence item, with the code and mapping claims marked "High" and the revenue conclusion marked "Medium."
"Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001" is identified as missing, and the submission states the matrix itself says "confirm Tares/ruling for legal use."
"Independent duty table — matrix has no duty column; 0% is declaration-sourced only."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Both codes share HS6 902110; they differ only in national tail digits, which the tariff matrix's Read Me says aren't expected to match across jurisdictions."
"The flag's comparator, \"Helios 90211090,\" is P1001's Helios commercial commodity code, which the master file itself calls migration-mapped and \"not customs-ruling status\"."
"Schema doesn't model code-system id, nomenclature version, or effective dates | canonical-schema-v0.3.md | High"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not raise this to the broker as an error."
"Reconfigure the comparator to compare within one nomenclature (or normalize to HS6) and make it code-system/date-aware".
"If legal certainty is needed, confirm via Swiss Tares/ruling, then close the flag as a documented cross-nomenclature artifact."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "no revenue at stake" is stronger than the cited support warrants because the submission acknowledges that the 0% duty evidence is declaration-sourced only and lacks an independent duty table.

"This is a cross-nomenclature false positive, not a broker error" is well supported as the leading explanation, but the submission also acknowledges that a Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling is missing, so the legal classification should remain conditional until verified.
"Declared code 90211000 is Switzerland's own approved code" relies on the matrix's characterization; the submission correctly notes that legal use should still be confirmed through Tares or a ruling.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The flag could still reflect an incorrect Swiss classification or a date/version issue despite the cross-nomenclature explanation, because the submission lacks an independent Swiss Tares or binding-ruling confirmation and does not identify the code-system and nomenclature versions attached to each value. The evidence makes this alternative less likely, not impossible.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the applicable Swiss Tares or binding-ruling entry, including the code-system and nomenclature version/effective date, and independently verify the duty treatment before closing the flag.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Preference = Yes is set on P1006, but \"Supplier support not linked in ClearView\"" is tied to "declaration.pdf; review_note.txt".
"SUP-02/P1006 (Ireland) is a lapsed document: valid_from 2025-01-01, valid_to 2025-07-31" is tied to "supplier_origin_register.csv".
"The same file itself states the search \"does not prove that no document exists outside the register\"" precisely records a source limitation.
"ERP/Helios carries manufacturing country (US)" and the workshop limitation are tied to "origin-workshop.md".

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly rejects "No document was found, so no valid document exists" because "the search only queried one key (SUP-02/P1006)".
It separately rejects "SUP-02's Irish declaration supports the claim" based on the document's expiry before "the 2025-09-18 entry".
It rejects "ERP shows US origin, so the claim is simply false" by distinguishing manufacturing country from preferential origin.
It rejects fraud escalation while identifying "four currently valid declarations for this exact product" as an alternative explanation rather than treating them as proof.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential-origin claim is not supported by anything in this packet, but it has not been disproved either" is appropriately limited.
"the reference file itself disclaims that this proves absence" accurately preserves the search limitation.
The submission identifies precise missing evidence: "Which supplier actually sourced this shipment of P1006" and "A current, valid supplier declaration covering the 2025-09-18 entry date".
It avoids treating the US ERP field as conclusive, stating that using it to clear preference is not sanctioned.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: It explains the data-lineage problem: "the packet never establishes which supplier actually sourced this shipment, so the right supplier may not have been searched at all".
It distinguishes system fields and purposes: "ERP/Helios captures manufacturing country, not preferential origin" and was "never designed to prove preference".
It identifies register incompleteness and alternate storage: declarations "sit in our category folders" and "the register isn't always kept current".
It correctly treats "Route (\"Origin hub → Ireland\") and consignee" as logistics facts rather than origin proof.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended control is proportionate: "do not clear it as preferential, and do not file it as fraud or issue any correction/disclosure yet".
The next steps are specific and reversible: "identify the actual sourcing supplier" and "request that supplier's current origin declaration plus the rule invoked".
The fallback is operationally clear: "If a valid document surfaces, apply preference; if none can be produced after that check, default to non-preferential treatment".
The submission recognizes the immediate financial context: "the line is already at 0.0% duty" while still preserving the documentation decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Given the line is already at 0.0% duty, holding it costs nothing financially" overstates the evidence: the packet may establish no immediate duty impact, but it does not establish that investigation, delay, or administrative handling has no cost.

"fraud requires showing no valid basis exists anywhere" is an overly broad legal/generalization. The evidence supports not escalating to a fraud finding now, but fraud analysis could also involve intent, knowledge, or misleading conduct rather than only proving that no valid basis exists anywhere.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be valid but unmatched because the shipment's actual sourcing supplier was not identified, the declaration may be stored in Procurement's category folders rather than the register, or the register may be stale. The available evidence therefore supports a documentation/linkage failure or unresolved sourcing issue more strongly than either a validly cleared claim or fraud.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the actual supplier and the governing preference agreement/rule first, then search both the register and Procurement's category folders for a declaration covering the 2025-09-18 entry, while replacing the categorical fraud statement with a narrower evidence-based explanation.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"Median receipt→release = 39.4h ... median lab_complete→release = 21.3h"

"30/215 RELEASED batches ... coa_status MISSING/INDEX_PENDING; 17/215 ... open_deviation=true"

Reason: Claims are tied to specific files, fields, counts, and medians, and use multiple evidence channels. The trace is strong but omits the qcore_release_ts hourly profile and does not establish the timestamp's event semantics.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "the number in circulation is likely the wrong clock, not the SOP's"
"the sample used to get any average excludes 42 still-open HOLD batches"
"both fields show values inconsistent with already-completed dispositions ... meaning they're current-state flags, not point-in-time records usable for timing"

Reason: The submission separates SOP definition, closed-sample selection, and current-state data quality, and tests several alternatives. It does not investigate the competing explanation that qcore_release_ts may be an interface or batch-commit timestamp, nor the 02:10 concentration.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "likely the wrong clock"
"that repetition looks like a fill value, not real events"
"confirm it isn't a placeholder"
"verify before using this as a KPI"

Reason: Uncertainty is generally claim-specific and source freshness is treated as decision-relevant. However, the submission sometimes moves from alignment or suspicious repetition toward causal interpretation without quantitatively bounding the alternatives.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Yes — verify before using this as a KPI"
"Get the current-as-of-now status of all 42 HOLD batches ... before it's dashboarded as a KPI"
"Confirm ... whether a genuine \"evidence complete\" timestamp exists"

Reason: It appropriately reframes the issue from simply calculating a KPI to validating its definition and data provenance, with practical follow-up actions. The recommendation would be stronger with an explicit reversible test using event/decision timestamps and success criteria, rather than emphasizing inclusion of open HOLDs before the start condition is known.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "lab_complete_ts is the right start point ... rejected"
"Averaging the closed 220 rows is representative enough ... rejected"
"coa_status/open_deviation reliably show evidence readiness ... rejected"

Reason: Three plausible hypotheses are explicitly rejected using SOP and data evidence, including a meaningful alternative about current-state versus point-in-time fields. The strongest competing explanation—release timestamps being interface commits or batch timing artifacts—is not tested.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Confirm in the data catalog ... whether a genuine \"evidence complete\" timestamp exists"
"Ask LabTrack/QCore owners why `lab_complete_ts` values postdate LabTrack's own stated snapshot"
"Get the current-as-of-now status of all 42 HOLD batches"

Reason: The requests are concrete and discriminating rather than generic. They are somewhat diffuse and omit the highest-value direct request for the definition of qcore_release_ts or an event log linking decision time to interface release time.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the number in circulation is likely the wrong clock" is plausible from the receipt-to-release alignment but is not established; the 36-hour figure could also reflect a valid operational receipt-to-release measure or timestamp/interface delay.

"35 of those already exceed 24h since receipt" is factually useful as backlog evidence, but it does not establish that those batches breached the SOP target, whose start is required-evidence availability rather than receipt.
"that repetition looks like a fill value, not real events" is a reasonable hypothesis, not a demonstrated conclusion; repeated timestamps could also arise from batch processing or extract behavior.
The assertion that closed-only averaging "understates true queue time" needs qualification because the correct cycle-start event for open HOLDs is not yet observed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent long cycle may be driven primarily by qcore_release_ts being an interface commit or batch-release timestamp, potentially concentrated at a scheduled time, rather than by the workflow start definition alone. The non-coherent LabTrack/QCore snapshots could further distort joins and current-state comparisons. This interpretation should be tested before changing operational processes or treating open-HOLD age as the KPI cycle.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request and analyze the timestamp definition or event log for required-evidence availability, disposition decision, and QCore interface release, including an hourly profile of qcore_release_ts. Use that evidence to decompose workflow delay from interface timing before calculating or redesigning the KPI.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “24 requests total $166,495.60 (qty×quote)” — tied to part_requests.csv and recomputation.

“8 requests ($20,536.31) have part number + a single other site with free, revision-matched, QUALIFIED_COMMON stock ≥ qty” — triangulated across part_requests.csv, spare_parts.csv, and part_restrictions.csv.
“MaintStar-global ... dated 2026-06-26 ... ProcureNet ... 2026-07-24” — tied to source_freshness.csv.
“Please do not turn every hit into a transfer recommendation...” — directly quoted from maintenance_email.txt.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “The search finds candidates, not approvals” separates retrieval from transfer authorization.
The submission tests identity, revision, qualification, reservation, and availability rather than treating description similarity as equivalence.

It triangulates stale availability, negative global availability with positive on-hand, revision mismatch, and critical reservations, and identifies live checks or engineering sign-off that would discriminate among explanations.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “12 ... have a real candidate but one unresolved check” and “Needs check” labels are appropriately claim-specific.
“MaintStar-global ... nearly a month older” and the request for “a live (not month-stale) stock check” recognize source-freshness uncertainty.
However, “8 ... are transfer-ready now,” “Firm saving is ~$20.5k,” and the recommendation to cancel POs remain too certain given the stale stock snapshot and potentially changing reservations.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Firm saving is ~$20.5k, not $166.5k” usefully separates candidate value from actionable value.
The recommendation distinguishes immediate candidates, unresolved checks, and non-transferable critical stock, and assigns specific follow-up questions.

The proposed immediate action to “raise the 8 transfers and cancel those POs” lacks a required live availability/reservation gate, creating operational risk despite the stale source being acknowledged.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects “A search hit is a transfer,” “available_qty_global = −1 means no stock,” “Same description family means interchangeable,” and “This is fundamentally a search-quality problem.”
It gives evidence for each rejection, including positive on-hand, revision differences, SITE_SPECIFIC_CHECK restrictions, critical reservations, and the email instruction.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: It requests prioritized discriminating evidence: manufacturer part numbers for the 11 blank-identity requests, live stock checks for HA-0022 and ME-0006, engineering sign-off on VLV-3722 revisions, site qualification confirmation, and current servo reservation status.
These requests are linked to explicit decision changes: candidates would become actionable, revision matches could be approved, or servo transfers could become possible.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 8 requests are “transfer-ready now” and the instruction to cancel their POs are overstated while the MaintStar snapshot is nearly a month older than ProcureNet; current stock, reservations, and receiving status should be confirmed first.
“Firm saving is ~$20.5k” is a candidate/actionable-value estimate rather than a firm realized saving until live availability, transfer execution, receipt, and PO cancellation are confirmed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analysis correctly identifies eight strong candidates, but none should be treated as fully actionable solely from the extracts: stale global availability or changed reservations could reduce the immediate set, while some of the twelve unresolved requests may become actionable after identity, revision, qualification, and live-stock validation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Insert a mandatory live MaintStar/ERP validation gate for each proposed transfer and PO cancellation—covering current free quantity, reservation/criticality, revision, qualification, and receipt status—then report confirmed transfers and savings separately from extract-based candidate value.
